subject.title: fix(reef): bound JSONL store file reads to prevent OOM on oversized audit/replay stores

question: Should an oversized Reef replay ledger fail closed until it is compacted, or should Reef provide a lossless bounded recovery mechanism before accepting traffic again?
rationale: This is a durable replay-protection and operator-recovery contract; source evidence shows that prefix truncation changes which persisted replay records are authoritative.

options.title: Fail closed for replay stores
options.body: Keep bounded audit-prefix reads, but reject or quarantine an oversized replay ledger until an operator compacts it so replay records are never silently ignored.

options.title: Implement lossless replay recovery
options.body: Use a bounded parsing/compaction design that preserves all replay decisions without loading the whole JSONL file into memory before accepting requests.

recommendation.title: Fail closed for replay stores
recommendation.body: Keep bounded audit-prefix reads, but reject or quarantine an oversized replay ledger until an operator compacts it so replay records are never silently ignored.
